\chapter{Eleven to a Thousand}
\label{ch:sa-eleven-to-a-thousand}
\hlchaptermodality{87}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can count eleven and twelve, and name twenty, a hundred and a thousand.}

Complete the last lesson of chapter 87: i can count eleven and twelve, and name twenty, a hundred and a thousand.
\end{chapteropening}

\section[ekādaśa]{\sk{एकादश} (ekādaśa) — eleven}

\label{lesson:SA-C87-eleven}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Sanskrit for time, then the Sanskrit for a moment.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \sk{एकादश}}
\textbf{\sk{एकादश}} (\emph{ekādaśa}) — \textquotedblleft{}eleven\textquotedblright{}: \textbf{\sk{एक}}, \textquotedblleft{}one\textquotedblright{}, with \textbf{\sk{दश}}, \textquotedblleft{}ten\textquotedblright{}. One and ten.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One plus ten.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ekādaśa}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ekādaśa}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{ekādaśa}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Sanskrit for time, then the Sanskrit for a moment, then say \emph{ekādaśa} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \sk{एकादश} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Eleven\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[dvādaśa]{\sk{द्वादश} (dvādaśa) — twelve}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \sk{द्वादश}}
\textbf{\sk{द्वादश}} (\emph{dvādaśa}) — \textquotedblleft{}twelve\textquotedblright{}: \textbf{\sk{द्वा}-}, \textquotedblleft{}two\textquotedblright{}, with \textbf{\sk{दश}}. The twelve months of a \textbf{\sk{संवत्सरः}}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
Two plus ten.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{dvādaśa}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{dvādaśa}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Sanskrit for a moment, then the Sanskrit for eleven, then say \emph{dvādaśa} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[viṃśatiḥ]{\sk{विंशतिः} (viṃśatiḥ) — twenty}

\label{lesson:SA-C87-twenty}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Sanskrit for eleven, then the Sanskrit for twelve.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \sk{विंशतिः}}
\textbf{\sk{विंशतिः}} (\emph{viṃśatiḥ}) — \textquotedblleft{}twenty\textquotedblright{}, a new word, not built from \textbf{\sk{दश}}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
A fresh word for two tens.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{viṃśatiḥ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{viṃśatiḥ}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Sanskrit for eleven, then the Sanskrit for twelve, then say \emph{viṃśatiḥ} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

Before the new one: say the Sanskrit for twelve, then the Sanskrit for twenty.

\textbf{\sk{शतम्}} (\emph{śatam}) — \textquotedblleft{}a hundred\textquotedblright{}. The English word \emph{hundred} is its distant cousin.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
Ten tens.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[sahasram]{\sk{सहस्रम्} (sahasram) — a thousand}

Ten hundreds.
